notes.title: Features of the incoming Math Challenge AR 1.1
notes.content:
[b]Math Challenge AR 1.1[/b] will be released next Thursday, July 10, the same day the [url=https://www.meta.com/en-gb/experiences/math-challenge-ar/23890991110527638/]Meta Quest version[/url] is released. 

Indeed, the Meta version will have an important new feature: a button that will allow you to disable the augmented reality mode, so that you can play in VR mode, that is, in an immersive way. With this, each player will be able to have both options, using the one that best suits him or her at any given moment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/be814302805426fb1c00ad8c3af96d35ccb958f3.png[/img]

On the other hand, in the attached screen you can see a new results window. This window shows the remaining points to reach the next level, as well as the static, dynamic, points, and starships panels needed to reach the next star. Remember that to get the stars it is necessary to have reached the level of those stars. All this is explained in the manual.

[b]Thank you very much.[/b]

notes.title: Math Challenge AR has been released!
notes.content:
[b]Math Challenge AR has already been released[/b]. This VR game presents a mathematical challenge for virtual reality users, but it aims to go one step further by presenting players with a series of challenges that they can configure themselves. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/ee3a15fc293855f8ceed8588a841ef1b3988e53e.jpg[/img]

Once you have completed the tutorial and prepared yourself in the training area, you can move on to the campaign. Or you can go directly to the campaign; everyone can play however they want. And if you activate the enemy option, solving math problems becomes a high-risk game.

For information on many aspects of the game, I recommend going to [url=https://mathchallengear.com]mathchallengear.com[/url], where [url=https://mathchallengear.com/about/manual-english/]the manual[/url] contains all the necessary information. The [url=https://mathchallengear.com/videos/]video section[/url] also contains a lot of important information. And, as always, practice makes perfect. 

[previewyoutube=U9kV9S-vb4M;full][/previewyoutube]

Oh, and one last thing: no calculators allowed. Use your brain. It's healthier.

Finally, this is an indie game developed by one person. My partner left this world last year, which was a brutal blow to me, and I had to continue the project on my own. Wherever she is, I know her support is still huge. I miss you so much, Rita.

Meta Quest Shop release is planned [url=https://www.meta.com/es-es/experiences/math-challenge-ar/23890991110527638/]for July 10th[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/6ae9d43ff12e1d5a3fa4c02bc049123a0782462b.jpg[/img]

And that's it. I'm sure you'll have a thousand suggestions. You can send them to the email: info at matchallengear.com. I'll be happy to fix any bugs you find and change any aspects you think might be of interest to players. There are many new features I have in my mind for the game that I think you will enjoy, at least I hope so!

[b]Thank you very much, and happy number hunting![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/cfa868e5c1a54498fa64ec42ec9ca738f03ef1c0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Some common questions about Math Challenge AR
notes.content:
[b]Math Challenge AR Steam version.[/b]

Math Challenge AR will be released on Steam on June 13, in a VR version under the SteamVR system. The game is, of course, the same as the version available on the Meta store, but within a virtual gaming environment.

In this article, we will discuss the answers to the most common questions about Math Challenge AR.

As for the questions, I have four articles written that cover many of the topics you mention. Here is a link to Steam with those articles. But, in summary:

[previewyoutube=U9kV9S-vb4M;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]1.- What are the differences between the Steam version and the Meta Quest store version?[/b]

The only difference is that in the Steam version, the external camera is not activated, which is replaced by a dome where the player plays in the same way as in the Meta Quest store version. Everything else is exactly the same.

[b]2.- What is the main appeal of Math Challenge AR? Why should I play it?
[/b]
The main appeal of the game is that it combines pure mental activity with the pressure to earn points and beat levels to get different prizes. If you add in the activation of enemies, then you also have to survive in an environment where you'll be attacked while trying to solve problems. Combining the calm needed to solve a math problem with combat against spaceships is definitely something that can be a big draw for many players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/ee3a15fc293855f8ceed8588a841ef1b3988e53e.jpg[/img]

[b]3.- Is it a complex game for those who have not used virtual reality glasses before?[/b]

Not at all. Players with little experience can play, as the game has an interactive tutorial and a detailed video with all the necessary information. There is also a manual on the website that details all aspects of the game.

[b]4.- What are the main elements that allow you to configure Math Challenge AR?
[/b]
The elements to be configured are divided into two parts: on the one hand, the type and complexity of the mathematical operations, including the type of problems, their level, whether you want decimals, whether you want negatives, whether you want to include equations, and the combination of all of these. 

On the other hand, you can configure aspects such as the playing area, the rotation of the operations (it is not the same to see a problem forwards as it is backwards, and that makes you lose time), and things like the speed of the numbers. All of this is combined to create your own scenario. In the campaign, the difficulty also increases, and prizes can only be obtained in the campaign.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/e3599566c92fa1b6334e55436023e16cf38197d5.jpg[/img]

[b]5.- How does the game ranking work?[/b]

The ranking is based on the following: first, the points. Only if you get a certain number of points can you get the prizes. Once you have them, the dynamic panels solved, the colored panels solved, and the enemy ships destroyed if you play in enemy mode are then taken into account. Each element has a star associated with it. To get all the stars, you must master all the elements. The ranking is only active in the campaign, not in training.

[b]6.- What are the bars at the bottom?[/b]

Two of the bars are typical of many games: health and energy. The third bar tells us how many points we need to reach the next achievement. The way it works is also simple: energy is consumed when you shoot, and it recharges when you hit the numbers. Energy spheres also appear that complete the charge. There are other spheres that regenerate health. And a third bar with a cap indicates how close you are to reaching the next level, but only in the campaign, since training is just that, training, according to what you have configured in the settings screens.

If you need more information, please don't hesitate [url=https://mathchallengear.com/about/manual-english/]to read the manual[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/6ae9d43ff12e1d5a3fa4c02bc049123a0782462b.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Release date and player characteristics
notes.content:
[previewyoutube="AxmZTF8F86g;full"][/previewyoutube][p] [i]

Note: Meta Quest Shop will be [url=https://www.meta.com/es-es/experiences/math-challenge-ar/23890991110527638/]available on July 10, 2025[/url].[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Let's set the scene: you've finally bought Math Challenge AR, and it's been the best decision of your life... Well, one of the best, let's not exaggerate.

Seriously, Math Challenge AR is the only math game where you can die while solving problems such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, or equations. That is, if you play with the enemy option activated. Otherwise, it's an augmented reality game where you set your own challenge in the training section, or complete the campaign, which is designed to become more complex and difficult with each new level.

So, who is Math Challenge AR intended for?

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/cfa868e5c1a54498fa64ec42ec9ca738f03ef1c0.jpg"][/img]
[b]1.- Math Students and everybody who wants to enjoy the game[/b]

Obviously, anyone can buy the game and enjoy it. Whether you're ten years old or a hundred. The game will be a challenge for everyone who wants to practice Mathematics.

[b]2.- Children.[/b]

Meta and other manufacturers of virtual and augmented reality glasses recommend that they be used from the age of ten. Personally, I think this is a good age, as a ten-year-old child is already mentally and physically developed enough to use virtual reality glasses. However, at the age of ten, I would recommend clear supervision by adults at all times. And short gaming sessions with breaks between sessions. Math Challenge AR is relatively intense, even in its version without enemies, because it wants to offer a challenge to the player. 

And it is clear that a ten-year-old child is still developing. The difficulty and type of problems should be configured by an adult before the child plays. Sessions should be short, no more than half an hour before a break.

From the age of twelve, children can be allowed to play for longer periods of time and configure the game to their liking. From the age of sixteen onwards, we know what happens: teenagers will tell their parents or guardians what to do and say.

[b]3.- Students with parental supervision.[/b]

I have been fortunate enough to hear the opinions of math teachers about the style of play proposed by Math Challenge AR. Some of the elements of the game were suggested by these teachers, such as the yellow and red sphere panels, where yellow is positive and red is negative, and the player has to choose the correct answer. Although it may seem simple, the effect of the spheres or dots causes the brain to work differently than it does when simply counting traditional mathematical operations.

For all these reasons, Math Challenge AR can be useful in schools and various training centers, including with children who require special attention. In fact, I have also received feedback from centers of this type.

In these cases, the teacher or tutor must always be in control of the system and decide the best way to help the children learn.

Math Challenge AR is, in any case, a complement to teaching, never a substitute, as is the case with all educational games.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/3488dff0eab15d3c8cee6b27b7405624950b17bc.jpg"][/img] 
[b]4.- Adults in general.[/b]

Practicing math skills is always useful. And to do so, an entertaining game will always help develop those skills.

[b]Why augmented reality?[/b]

Some may wonder why the game was made with augmented reality and not virtual reality, with a setting full of famous mathematicians such as Leibniz or Newton throwing bricks at you if you get a sum wrong.

I like that question (which no one has ever asked me before). The answer is very simple: a virtual environment poses a greater danger to gameplay, as you cannot see the real environment, and it increases the likelihood of dizziness and vertigo. Math Challenge AR has been designed in augmented reality to avoid these problems, which I myself suffer from, by the way, when I play standing up.

In the end, Math Challenge AR is an Augmented Reality game with Math inside, but where the player will have to sweat to win. And that's another way of seeing Mathematics!

[b]Hope you enjoy the game. Regards!
[/b]
[/p]

notes.title: Scoring system in Math Challenge AR
notes.content:
[b]A math game? Get that out of my sight![/b]

Indeed, a math game is not a Civilization, or a GTA, or a DOOM. And I'm not talking about the million-dollar budget to develop it. In fact, a math game could cost two hundred million dollars. But who would buy it?

[previewyoutube=WYp_IxVooJY;full][/previewyoutube]

Actually, there are people interested in math games and educational games, I know from experience. Not many, but there are people who consider that a math game can complement the learning of this discipline in children, and also adults. It is clear that a game alone will never replace a teacher, that is indisputable. But it can be a support.

That's why Math Challenge AR is an augmented reality educational game, which aims to go beyond the classic math games. The goal is to turn mathematics into the protagonist of a puzzle-type game, but also of action.

To achieve this, the player has two elements at his disposal: the training area, where he can configure the game to his liking according to the configuration screens, and, of course, the campaign area. There the challenge is to overcome all possible levels, up to... as far as the player wants. There is no limit. Let's say that x tends to infinity, if you allow me this bad joke.

[b]The calculation of progress.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/21c9ff4e982160a78ad0c77534be3b18b2302393.png[/img]

If Math Challenge AR looks like a weird game to you, wait until you see the scoring system. In general, many games have a progress bar, which indicates how close the player is to reaching the next level. In Math Challenge AR the same thing happens; there is a bar (the one below) that indicates when you are going to get the next prize (or award as it's called in the game), within the sixteen possible ones. The more the bar is filled, the closer to the award.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/0bf856626faeae6205c9d8b7bdc5692c7470d4eb.png[/img]

[b]But there is a problem: the bar can go backwards.[/b]

That's right. The bar can go backwards. Let's see it with an example: imagine you are playing at level 5 of the campaign. In level 4 you reached 400 points. You are not going to lose those points. But in this game you have 50 points. Well: if you start making mistakes, the game will not only not give you new points; it will take away the ones you already have.

What twisted mind can design something like that? Mine, of course. If I was made to suffer with math when I was a kid, my goal now is to make others suffer with math. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/8eae1c13b0efafd701fba7fb0e6d00a162b43c24.png[/img]

The formula you can see in this image indicates how the score is calculated. This score is dynamic, it is constantly recalculated according to your actions, your successes, and your failures. Basically, the static panels are solved by shooting the correct numbers that move around the stage. For example, if you have a 13+5, you should shoot an 8, and then a 1. If you shoot other numbers that will subtract points. I have been benevolent and there will be no negative scores. But I could have chosen that.

That will end the static panel, moving on to the next one. When you've finished all the static panels, you've finished the level.

The dynamic panels show three solutions, and they appear randomly. You must choose the correct option before the panel disappears. If it disappears, it will be counted as a “not executed”. If you shoot wrong, it will be counted as “wrong”.

With the point panels you must also shoot at the correct option, or it will take away points.
And the spaceships, well, the spaceships will be shooting at you and taking lives. You must destroy them if you want to survive. Bonus adds points by shooting fast to numbers, and infinity when this symbol appears in vertical.

Another thing: remember that you can manually generate dynamic panels, point panels, and enemy spaceships, as shown in the image you can see here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/cfa868e5c1a54498fa64ec42ec9ca738f03ef1c0.jpg[/img]

That is, if you are one of those who like to really suffer, you can go pressing the buttons and generating panels and even enemy spaceships (if you have activated the enemy mode) constantly, until your head explodes.

Remember. The static panels, the ones that require the numbers, are the ones that, when you finish them, allow you to finish the level. If you don't finish them, the level doesn't end, until the maximum time of the level runs out. If the time runs out and you have not finished, you lose all the points again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/82c068be83a82300bdd1836d61fb33ff0797f36c.jpg[/img]

All this ends up allowing you to calculate the total amount of points. Successes have positive multiplier factors, and mistakes have negative multiplier factors. In the training you always start from zero and there is no possibility to get prizes. In the campaign you accumulate points from the previous level, and it will allow you to unlock awards.

Oh, one last thing: shooting fast at the floating numbers allows a bonus. There is a second counter that changes color. The sooner you shoot the next number, the more points.

[b]Good  math hunting![/b]

notes.title: Training mode and Campaign mode in Math Challenge AR
notes.content:
Math Challenge AR has two game modes, which we will see below, and which have some important differences that are worth knowing. Leaving aside the typical tutorial of course, which you can run whenever you want. Let's take a look at it below.

[previewyoutube=AxmZTF8F86g;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Training mode.[/b]

The training mode allows the player to configure the game to his liking, with the exact parameters that he decides at each moment. To do this, just enter the configuration screen, adapt the game elements, and start training. Some of the parameters in the configuration screen are self-explanatory. Others deserve an explanation. All of this can be read in the game manual, where the function of each of these parameters is explained in detail.

Once the player is satisfied with a configuration, at the start of a training session the player will play with those parameters set. In that way, the player can modify the type of mathematical operations, the maximum playing time, whether there will be negatives or decimals in the operations, how many digits each operation will have, or more general things such as the speed of rotation of the static panels, or the speed at which the numbers move. Even if you want some help during the game, something that can come in handy for the little ones in the house.

The training mode stores the results of a game session, and displays them at the end of the training session. You can also view those results at any time from the settings screen.

What training mode does not do is earn achievements. Achievements are reserved for the campaign mode, which we will see below.

[b]Campaign mode in Math Challenge AR.[/b]

The campaign mode in Math Challenge AR works in a different way than the training mode. What it does is to start at level one, and reconfigures the game internally so that the difficulty increases with each new level. It is important to note that it does not touch the settings on the configuration screen. What it does is to ignore those parameters, and thus starts a campaign that, in the first levels, will be very easy, but will become more complex during the development of the campaign.

How many levels are there in the campaign? There is no limit. It is true that after certain levels the game will not be more complex and difficult, but overcoming each level will be a challenge. Of course, the player can continue passing levels as long as he wants, and there will be no limit.

[b]The awards associated with the campaign mode.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/2425fd6cab24cf2ded0a3083faf3301b36266c32.png[/img]

With the development of the campaign the player will go through different ranks, until reaching the maximum. There are sixteen possible ranks.

[b]Patch:[/b] it is obtained by earning points. The campaign bar with the cap symbol will be filled as the player gets closer to the next award. When it arrives, the award will be activated and the bar will start filling up again.

The stars in each patch will only be visible if the point level of the patch has been reached. The colors indicate different awards:

* Blue: activated when a number of solved static panels has been exceeded. Remember that the static panels must be solved to finish the training at the level of the campaign you are playing.
* Green: it is activated when a number of dynamic panels have been passed.
* Yellow: it is activated when you have passed a number of point panels.
* Red: activated when a number of enemy ships have been destroyed. This requires playing with the enemies mode logically activated.

It is important to note that, even if a patch has been activated, the stars will not appear until the number of elements necessary to activate that star has been obtained. But, if you have not obtained the points to activate a patch, the stars, even if they are active, will not appear. You will have to combine points and stars to get all the prizes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/21c9ff4e982160a78ad0c77534be3b18b2302393.png[/img]

The upper bar controls the power you have for your lasers. The middle one your health. And the last one, visible only in Campaign, indicates the points you need to get the next awards.

[b]Ending the game.
[/b]
Oh, and one important thing: if you run out of health in the game during a level, all points earned from that level are lost. Not the previous ones, but the ones earned in that level. So you will have to finish that level to be able to add up the points.

And that's all on the subject of Math Challenge AR's training and campaign modes. Now it's up to you, let math be with you!

notes.title: Mathematics, a voyage to undestand the world
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

In this first entry I want to salute all lovers of science, knowledge, and Star Trek fans. Well, Star Wars fans too. Hey, I saw Star Wars in 1978. Maybe you can't say that! It was great! By the way, I loved Andor 1st and 2nd seasons. A Masterpiece, or at least it seems so to me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/c8da9161bb5eb4c5fa0253e374f5bf06eb69bff8.jpg[/img]

Ok, let's get down to business. Until the game is released, I'm going to make several informative posts about Math Challenge AR, the augmented reality game that combines mathematics with action and even combat, if you activate the enemies option of the game. But, in this first entry I'm going to get a little more serious, to present you an [url=https://mathchallengear.com/mathematics-a-voyage-to-understand-the-world/]article that you have in the link[/url], and that has little or nothing to do with the game, but with the importance of mathematics.

You see: I, like many other children, had a lot of problems with mathematics. It was a nightmare for me. But, little by little, with the help of great teachers, and with a lot of effort, I began to realize that mathematics is like a game. It has basic rules, medium rules, and advanced rules. If you don't know the basic rules, the middle and advanced rules will be impossible to understand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/f6c24b5538a03f49fa1103dc8e1665df44abcd5f.png[/img]

Based on that youthful experience I wanted to reflect on learning mathematics. And don't think I'm a math genius now. Far from it; I have a lot of difficulties. But I overcame my fears, and I was able to pass the exams that allowed me to develop a professional career as a computer engineer. Most importantly, however, I was not useless at math, as some people told me; I just needed patience, work, and some help. When I had them, I overcame all barriers.

There are many young people in my situation. That's why I want to encourage them to struggle, strive, and work hard. It will not be easy. But, with a little help, I'm sure they will be able to overcome any barriers as well. If I did it, so can they.

In the next post I will talk about the Math Challenge AR game. Remember that there is already a lot of information and videos on the web. Thank you very much!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/0bf856626faeae6205c9d8b7bdc5692c7470d4eb.png[/img]
